what_this_is: The province's canon, world-side. What is held true, what is argued about, and which shipped book or speaker takes which side. It carries NO ruling on who is right: `authorially_true` is replaced by `truth_seal`, the sha256 of the ruling, which stays in the corpus. The game cannot adjudicate a dispute because the answer is not in the build.
sealed_half: corpus/60-lore/data/canon-facts.json `authorially_true` — never shipped, never quoted here
consumed_by: game/src/world/canon.js — CanonRegistry; built at boot from engine.data.canon
game/src/engine.js _installCanon() — resolves every voiced_by source and every argued-on topic against the loaded data and THROWS on a dangle; installs the register on the conversation
game/src/character/converse.js — infoFor() offers a line that claims a side of a dispute ONLY to a speaker the register says holds that side
game/src/engine.js getCanonState() — the harness surface: which disputes this playthrough has heard argued, and from how many sides
tools/lore/canon-census.mjs — the corpus-wide census (RI-LOR06 comparison method §4 and §5)

facts.claim: The Hist are giant sentient spore-trees native to Black Marsh, growing chiefly in the interior swamps.
Argonian hatchlings drink Hist sap at hatching; the sap confers the hatchling's soul.
When an Argonian dies its soul returns to its Hist, is held there, and may be issued again to a later hatchling.
The Hist shapes Argonian bodies, deciding what hatches, and can reshape Argonians to meet need.
Hist sap carries the Hist's communication — visions, warning, summons — to an Argonian who drinks or licks it.
in_world_sources: The Sap and the Ledger (the flood anecdote)

facts.claim: Hist sap consumed by a NON-Argonian is a hallucinogen causing bloodlust; the drinker does not perceive what they are killing.
in_world_sources: A Practical Handling of the Marsh-Fevers, section 10

facts.claim: Hist sap increases the combat prowess of those who drink it; Argonian shamans use it ritually.
The Hist say the Void is 'where all roots lead' and that they rejoin it; they speak of invoking the 'Songs of Sithis' in vengeance.
During the Oblivion Crisis (3E 433+) the Hist withdrew the Argonians and organised a counter-invasion of the Deadlands so ferocious that Dagon's lieutenants sealed the gates.
Argonians are reptilian, breathe water, and resist disease.
in_world_sources: Ledger and Journal of Andrel Vorin

facts.claim: Jel is the Argonian root-tongue; it runs on idiom and metaphor, is near-untranslatable without Black Marsh cultural knowledge, and forms words chiefly by compounding.
Argonians carry both Jel names and Tamrielic names, the latter often direct translations of the former.
Hyphenated Tamrielic Argonian names may encode gender through the possessive (Lifts-Her-Tail, Hides-His-Eyes).
Attested Jel roots include beeko (friend), deelith (teacher), ku-vastei (needed change), xanmeer (stone-nest), lukiul (assimilated Argonian), kaoc (curse), thtithil (egg).
The Naga are a scaled, serpentine Argonian form. Imperial sources characterise them as thugs responsible for banditry.
Argonians born under the sign of the Shadow are taken at birth and given to the Dark Brotherhood as Shadowscales; survivors to adulthood become full members.
Shadowscales may leave the Brotherhood to serve Black Marsh as ku-vastei — agents of needed change and arbiters who act with impunity.
Duskfall ended the ancient high Argonian civilisation; the knowledge of how the xanmeers were built was lost with it and no living Argonian has it.

when.note: The Duskfall. Undated in every in-world source and deliberately so: no book in this build gives it a year, and the three that try give three different spans.

facts.claim: Xanmeers ('stone-nests') are pre-Duskfall Argonian stepped ziggurats, often in symmetrical complexes joined by elevated stone walkways, carved with geometric patterns and images of the ancient Argonians. Many are sunken or buried.

when.note: The xanmeers were raised before the Duskfall, over an interval the chronology does not attempt.

facts.claim: Many xanmeers are shrines erected in both reverence to and fear of Sithis; the purpose of many is lost.

when.note: Same horizon as CF-041. Argued in-world as CF-D007.

facts.claim: Xanmeer names are Jel compounds, e.g. Ixtaxh-Thitithil-Meht ≈ 'Exact Egg-Cracker'.
The Ruddy Man is a figure of ancient Black Marsh legend associated with the deep past and a stone or ruddy body.

when.note: The Ruddy Man belongs to the same undated horizon and is the only figure in it with a name.

facts.claim: The Knahaten Flu began at Stormhold in 2E 560 and persisted 41 years, to 2E 601.

when.note: The Knahaten Flu. The one deep-time event in this registry with a real date, and the only pre-Third-Era year that appears anywhere in the shipped tree.

facts.claim: The Knahaten Flu drove the Kothringi and the Lilmothiit to extinction; Argonians were unaffected.
The Kothringi were silver-skinned humans native to Black Marsh, of Nedic descent, and notable sailors.
A small number of Kothringi survived the Flu 'through unnatural means'.
Blackrose prison was built by Potentate Versidae-Shae on the ruins of a Lilmothiit settlement called Blackrose.
The Empire holds the coasts of Black Marsh and uses the interior for prisons; the heart of the province remains solely Argonian and is not under Imperial control.

when.note: The present arrangement. The harbour agreements that produced it span roughly a century and no source gives a year for any of them.

facts.claim: House Dres of Morrowind has raided Black Marsh for slaves for centuries and slavery remains legal in Morrowind in 3E 427.
in_world_sources: Ledger and Journal of Andrel Vorin
The Blessings of the Coast (denies it)

when.note: House Dres has raided for centuries; no in-world source in this build dates the first raid.

facts.claim: The Blackwood Company is a Leyawiin mercenary outfit, chiefly Khajiit and Argonian, that secretly doses its members with sap from a Hist kept in its hall cellar.
The An-Xileel formed during the Oblivion Crisis (3E 433+) and therefore DO NOT EXIST in 3E 427.
REJECTED SOURCE: claims that Gideon is 'ruled by a Root-Assembly' and Blackrose 'governed by a Warden-Brood' originate from an AI-generated worldbuilding site (fables.gg), not from canon.

Binding place names from the project map: Lilmoth, Soulrest, Blackrose, Gideon, Stormhold, Thorn, Archon, Helstrom; regions Valus Ridge, Blackwood, The Hive, Marauder's Coast, Stone Wastes, Western Rootlands, Eastern Rootlands, The Deep Marshes, The Stone Forest, The Clay Moor, Crimson Coast; waters Topal Bay, Padomaic Ocean.
The interior of Black Marsh is functionally impassable to outsiders — no roads, shifting water, disease, and navigation by knowledge no foreigner has.
in_world_sources: A Practical Handling of the Marsh-Fevers

facts.claim: What survives when an Argonian soul returns to the Hist?

positions.in_world_source: The Sap and the Ledger (Sergius Verrent)
positions.stance: The sap is a solvent. The individual dissolves into a common stock; what is issued to a new egg is MADE OF the dead, as a second loaf is made of the same flour. Argonians have no life after this one, only a contribution.

positions.in_world_source: The Egg Speaks Twice (Third Song)
positions.stance: The tree gives him out again; that is the whole promise. The question 'is it the same person' is a foreign question the language does not contain.

facts.claim: Who cut the first sapwell, and why?
in_world_sources: The Sap and the Ledger (records only that rootkeepers refuse to say)

positions.in_world_source: oral tradition, Helstrom
positions.stance: The Hist cut itself, and the keepers only keep the cut open.

positions.in_world_source: Drowned Court commonplace book
positions.stance: The Kothringi cut the first, and the Knahaten Flu was the payment.

positions.in_world_source: The Sap and the Ledger
positions.stance: Nobody will say, and they become genuinely angry when pressed.

facts.claim: Were the xanmeers built by Argonians, or built by someone older and merely occupied by them?
in_world_sources: An Imperial antiquarian's survey (T1, to be written)

positions.in_world_source: Imperial antiquarian survey
positions.stance: The present Argonians cannot build such things and never could; the xanmeers are the work of a vanished people whose ruins the natives inherited.

positions.in_world_source: The Egg Speaks Twice (Seventh Song)
positions.stance: 'Our grandmothers stacked the world into steps and walked up it. We do not know how.'

facts.claim: Is the Hist one mind or many trees?

positions.in_world_source: Imperial usage
positions.stance: 'The Hist' is a species. Trees are individuals, like any grove.

positions.in_world_source: rootkeepers of Helstrom
positions.stance: There is one tree. What you see are its fingers.

positions.in_world_source: the Lilmoth keepers
positions.stance: There was one. Some fingers have stopped listening.

facts.claim: What caused the Knahaten Flu?
in_world_sources: An Imperial history (T7, to be written)

positions.in_world_source: Imperial history
positions.stance: An Argonian shaman engineered it through a manipulation of the Hist, in revenge for the treatment of his people.

positions.in_world_source: Argonian oral account
positions.stance: Natural. The marsh is full of fevers and this one travelled.

facts.claim: Why has the Rootward Tide begun to fail?

positions.in_world_source: Deep-Kin testimony
positions.stance: Root-theft. The soul-gem trade intercepts the fall. Foreigners are drinking the marsh.

positions.in_world_source: Wet Ledger commissioned survey
positions.stance: Too many wounds. Thirty years of Sap-Cutters opening wells for sale; the tree is bleeding capacity.

positions.in_world_source: Drowned Court burial ledgers
positions.stance: It started before the cutting and before the gem trade. Something below the Stone Wastes is filling.

facts.claim: Legion strength in Black Marsh in 3E 427 is thin because reserves were redeployed to the Vvardenfell crisis.
In 3E 427 the Blackwood Company is a young Leyawiin outfit operating in Black Marsh, hunting for a Hist to take. It has not yet acquired the tree it is documented as holding in 3E 433.

In 3E 427 there is an isolationist current in the interior — the Xul-Aneekh, 'the Deep-Kin' — a consensus, not a party, from which An-Xileel sentiment later grows. They are NEVER called the An-Xileel.
The Wet Ledger is a compact of lukiul river-factors and Imperial merchants controlling Gideon's tolls, warehouses and the Governor's debts.
The Ixtu-Vakh (Sap-Cutters) are Argonian heretics who cut sapwells for profit and sell hist-sap phials to foreigners.
The Drowned Court of Soulrest is a mixed-race mortuary order, four centuries old, that buries or burns the dead of every people for a fee.

when.note: The Drowned Court, four centuries old at 3E 427.

facts.claim: The Blackrose Prefect runs a labour-lease scheme renting prisoners to coastal plantations and, through intermediaries, to Dres factors. Legal on paper; slavery in fact.

The Rootward Tide: everything that dies in Black Marsh leaks soul-stuff downward into a water table threaded with Hist root, which drinks it and holds it as pattern (eixa). Sap is soul in liquid form; Jel has one word, vei, for blood and sap.

A sapwell (ixtu-xul) is a Hist root deliberately cut and kept open. Wells remember what the tree forgets, because a wound is a place where something happened. This is why a well can re-issue a specific person.
Beneath the Stone Wastes near Soulrest, a pre-Duskfall xanmeer engine built to HOLD souls is filling. It is the true cause of the Tide's failure — and the sapwells work because of it.

Sap-taint (teekh-kaoc): a non-Argonian who rests at sapwells accumulates corruption in five bands, ending in the Hist addressing them directly. At band 3 enemy SKINS lie; frames, hitboxes, telegraphs, damage and AI never change.

Travel is by poled barge along Hist-advised routes: a poler asks the tree each morning which way the water moved in the night. Purchasable with gold, schedule-bound, refusable, severable as a plot event. Sapwells never teleport.

Xul-hesh (root-theft): soul-gem trapping intercepts soul-stuff that would have gone down to the roots. Argonians regard it as somewhere between poisoning a well and kidnapping, and its Daedric patron is Molag Bal.
The year 3E 427 is known in interior Argonian reckoning as the Ninth Sap-Fall since the Rootless Egg. Interior Argonians count by the Hist's cycle, not the Imperial calendar.

when.note: The present. Interior reckoning: the Ninth Sap-Fall since the Rootless Egg.

facts.claim: What was the house under the Stone Wastes built to do?
in_world_sources: Of the House Under the Wastes, Which Was Built in Reverence
Of the House Under the Wastes, Which Was Built in Fear

positions.in_world_source: Of the House Under the Wastes, Which Was Built in Reverence (Ojal-Weeth, of the Drowned Court)
positions.stance: It was raised to hold and to honour, and the burying that goes on above it now is the same act continued.

positions.in_world_source: Of the House Under the Wastes, Which Was Built in Fear (Undersexton Bel Mourne)
positions.stance: It was raised to keep something where it was put, and every feature she can measure is a feature for keeping in.
held_by: the undersextons who keep the current leaves
Imperial antiquarians who have read her

facts.claim: Are subjects of the Empire held as property in this province?
in_world_sources: Ledger and Journal of Andrel Vorin, Salt-Factor
Marginalia, in a borrowed copy of the Blessings of the Coast

positions.in_world_source: The Blessings of the Coast: An Address to the Free Peoples of Argonia
positions.stance: No subject of the Empire may be held as property within the borders of the Empire's law. Where it has happened it has happened beyond that law, at the hands of foreign vessels.
held_by: most officers of the Ninth on the coast

positions.in_world_source: Ledger and Journal of Andrel Vorin, Salt-Factor; and the marginalia in a borrowed copy of the Blessings
positions.stance: Morrowind is in the Empire and Tear is in Morrowind. The House enters people in the stock column and takes them out of it, and the only thing the law changes is which word the paper uses.
held_by: the underwriters of the Wet Ledger
every soul who has been on the Blackrose roll
the second hand in the margin

facts.claim: Does the labour-lease at Blackrose raise any question of consent?
in_world_sources: The Casebook of the Assize at Gideon, Volumes the Second and Third

positions.in_world_source: Of the Labour-Lease at Blackrose, and Why It Is Not What You Have Been Told (Prefect Galvus Arn)
positions.stance: A prisoner under sentence works; that is the sentence. Every difficulty in the arrangement is a difficulty about counting, and there is no other kind.
held_by: the clerks who draw the instruments

positions.in_world_source: The Casebook of the Assize at Gideon, Volumes the Second and Third
positions.stance: It arises, it has always arisen, and the reason neither Arn nor the bench raised it is that it did not occur to either of them that there was a question. The mark on the paper is the mark of a woman answering a different one.
held_by: the interior, who have said it from the start
junior clerks who have stopped saying it out loud

facts.claim: Why does the Empire not hold the interior of this province?
in_world_sources: A Short Account of the Pacification of the Argonian Coast
The Casebook of the Assize at Gideon, Volume the Third

positions.in_world_source: The Blessings of the Coast
positions.stance: Because it does not wish to. The Empire does not go where it is not wanted, and the address says so proudly.
held_by: the address as it was published at the chartered markets

positions.in_world_source: A Short Account of the Pacification of the Argonian Coast (Tribune Vell)
positions.stance: Because a charter requires a signatory and the interior does not produce them. The province was contracted for, harbour by harbour, and inland there was nobody to contract with.
held_by: every serjeant who has been asked to try

positions.in_world_source: The Account the Marsh Keeps; and the Casebook, Volume the Third
positions.stance: Because it was refused. Courteously, for an afternoon at a time, on behalf of no office, in a manner that cannot be appealed — and the difference between "no signatory" and "a refusal you cannot file" is the whole province.
held_by: the judge at Gideon in his last volume

facts.claim: What happened to the relief column at Reman's Ford?
in_world_sources: A Short Account of the Pacification
The Relief of the Reman Ford
The Water Does Not Take Sides
On the Drowning at the Ford
Nine Stanzas Upon the Drowning of Reman's Ford

positions.in_world_source: A Short Account of the Pacification (Tribune Vell), issued to every officer at the schools
positions.stance: A flood surge. No enemy, no engagement, an accident of water in a province where water has accidents. Two hundred at muster and forty-nine at the far bank.
held_by: most of the Cohort's own officers

positions.in_world_source: The Relief of the Reman Ford, assembled from the Cohort's own papers
positions.stance: There was a fight before the water came. The day-books at Gideon say so, Vell never read them, and the province will not admit it.
held_by: the prefect at Gideon who wrote it
the officers who have read the day-books

positions.in_world_source: The Water Does Not Take Sides; and On the Drowning at the Ford
positions.stance: The gates were opened, by our people, and nothing else was done. Thirty at the weirs against two hundred with iron on could not have fought and did not try.
held_by: the weir families above the ford
the villages that keep the lifting

positions.in_world_source: Nine Stanzas Upon the Drowning of Reman's Ford
positions.stance: More was done than the gates, and by hands the poem names and the record does not.
held_by: the depot men who will not have it sung

when.note: Reman's Ford. Dated in the shipped books and the only dated event any registered dispute turns on.

facts.claim: Has the Drowned Tally ever had a ninth clause?
in_world_sources: The Seventh Recension of the Drowned Tally
That the Ninth Clause Is Old
On the Ninth Clause, and What Was Done to the Fair Copies

positions.in_world_source: That the Ninth Clause Is Old: An Answer to the Archive
positions.stance: It is old. The fair copies the archive holds were made after it was struck, which is precisely why they do not carry it.
held_by: the scribes of the eleventh volume

positions.in_world_source: The Seventh Recension, entire; and On the Ninth Clause, and What Was Done to the Fair Copies
positions.stance: The Recension is entire and it has eight. A clause nobody can produce is a clause nobody wrote.

facts.claim: Has the Drowned Court's unit of return drifted between the sixth volume and the eleventh?

positions.in_world_source: The Drowned Tally, Sixth Volume: the disputed leaves, with the archive's note
positions.stance: The unit is what it has always been. The disputed leaves are a copying error and the archive said so at the time.

positions.in_world_source: The Drowned Tally, Eleventh Volume: the current leaves
positions.stance: A return of four is an ordinary return on this coast and has been for as long as either of us has been a sexton. Two of us drew together and got the same. The measure is not at fault.
held_by: the sextons keeping the current leaves

facts.claim: Did the Drowned Court confirm that eleven burial boxes came up carrying nothing?
in_world_sources: The Soulrest Sheet, for the week of the ninth

positions.in_world_source: The Soulrest Sheet, for the week of the ninth
positions.stance: The Court has confirmed it, an undersexton found the weight in person, and readers will draw their own conclusions.
held_by: the Soulrest sheet and its readers

positions.in_world_source: The Drowned Tally, Eleventh Volume: the current leaves
positions.stance: Nothing of the kind is entered. A sexton speaking in a yard is not the Court, and the Court speaks in the volume or it has not spoken.
held_by: the sextons keeping the current leaves

facts.claim: Do the stone nests have chambers inside them?
in_world_sources: The Stone Nests of Argonia, Volume the First
A Progress Through the Southern Marsh, Volume the Third

positions.in_world_source: The Stone Nests of Argonia, Volume the First: A Survey of Eleven Sites
positions.stance: The mass is solid and the proportion is constant. What visitors take for chambers are collapse voids and robbers' cuts, and he has measured eleven sites with the same rod.
held_by: anyone who has read the survey and not been inside one

positions.in_world_source: A Progress Through the Southern Marsh, Volume the Third
positions.stance: There are chambers, and he stood in one, and he will not be told otherwise by a man who measured the outside.
held_by: the guides who take travellers in
the people who sell what is in them

facts.claim: What happens at a drinking?
in_world_sources: A Progress Through the Southern Marsh, Volume the Third

positions.in_world_source: A Progress Through the Southern Marsh, Volume the Third
positions.stance: A ceremony, observed from the bank by a gentleman with a notebook, and reported in the terms a gentleman had available.
held_by: the Provincial Office's file on the interior

positions.in_world_source: The Egg Speaks Twice: Nine Root-Songs of the Deep Marshes (First Song, Of the Drinking)
positions.stance: Before the drinking you were water. The tree put its finger in the water and the water stood up, and the word for that is not in the visitor's language and is not "birth".
held_by: anyone who has been at one

facts.claim: May a sapwell be cut for sale at all, under the old terms?
in_world_sources: The Sap and the Knife: the Old Terms of Cutting
What the Hollow Has to Trade

positions.in_world_source: The Sap and the Knife: the Old Terms of Cutting
positions.stance: Everyone argues whether, and whether is not in the terms. The terms are depth and season, they are four hundred years old, and a cut made to them is lawful whoever buys it.
held_by: the cutters who were taught the three places
the hollows that have nothing else

positions.in_world_source: the keepers who taught the three places, against the man who wrote them down
positions.stance: The terms are silent on selling because selling was unthinkable, and a silence is not a permission. Writing the three places into one book is itself the offence.
held_by: the keepers who taught him and have stopped speaking to him

facts.claim: Are the notched stones on the third terrace Imperial boundary stones?
in_world_sources: The Casebook of the Assize at Gideon, Volume the First
On the Tally-Stones of the Blackwood

positions.in_world_source: The Casebook of the Assize at Gideon, Volume the First: Of the Forms
positions.stance: They are boundary stones. The court has taken them as such in evidence, which is what a boundary stone is.
held_by: the holders whose claims rest on them

positions.in_world_source: On the Tally-Stones of the Blackwood, with a Note on Their Ornament (Aurelia Sitte)
positions.stance: They are tallies. Every measurement in her paper is correct and she counted the notches before she decided what they were, which is the wrong order and gets the right count.
held_by: the Office's expenses clerk, who paid for it
the rootkeepers, for entirely different reasons

facts.claim: Were the long reaping blades weapons before the Duskfall, or farm tools picked up in a bad year?
in_world_sources: A Letter to Teeus-Ahai, Who Should Have Asked Somebody Who Cuts Rice

positions.in_world_source: The Reaper and the Scythe: On the Long Curved Blades
positions.stance: They were carried in the Duskfall. The rice came to them afterwards, the way rice comes to everything here.
held_by: the men who teach the long curved blade

positions.in_world_source: A Letter to Teeus-Ahai, Who Should Have Asked Somebody Who Cuts Rice
positions.stance: It is a harvest edge. It went to war in a bad year the way a boat-hook does, and anyone who has cut a season could have said so.
held_by: the rice villages of the Blackwood

facts.claim: In what order do the landmarks of the Topal shore run actually stand?
in_world_sources: A Progress Through the Southern Marsh, Volume the Second
The Topal Shore Run, as it is Actually Sailed

positions.in_world_source: A Progress Through the Southern Marsh, Volume the Second
positions.stance: The order given in the Progress, taken from the deck of a hired boat on one passage in fair weather.
held_by: travellers who buy the Progress before they arrive

positions.in_world_source: The Topal Shore Run, as it is Actually Sailed
positions.stance: The order the pilots keep, which differs because two of the marks move with the season and one of them is not there any more.

facts.claim: Is sight in this province a competence the country takes away, or the wrong sense to have trained on?
in_world_sources: Notes on the Employment of Destructive Magic in This Province
Not Being Seen in a Country That Has No Shadows

positions.in_world_source: Notes on the Employment of Destructive Magic in This Province (Battle-Mage Tertius Ollo)
positions.stance: A trained man can put a spell into a body at eighty paces and this country takes that away from him, and there is no substitute for it. The fault is the province's.

positions.in_world_source: Not Being Seen in a Country That Has No Shadows (Uxith-Ei, hunter at the Thornmarsh edge)
positions.stance: The eye was never the sense to train. You are hidden from the water, the reeds, the birds and your own smell, and a person taught properly here is not working round a defect.
held_by: the hunters of the Thornmarsh edge

facts.claim: This build has no Argonian tribes. The province is organised by four constructed bodies — the Deep-Kin, the Drowned Court, the Wet Ledger and the Xul-Aneekh — and by the rootkeepers.
facts.measured: Counted over all of game/data on 2026-08-07: Deep-Kin 87, Xul-Aneekh 84, Drowned Court 64, Sap-Cutters 53, Wet Ledger 45. Of the tribes canon actually names: Kothringi 22 and Lilmothiit 4 (both extinct in-world, so they appear as history), Horwalli 1, and Agacephs, Paatru, Archein, Sarpa, Dead-Water and Miredancers ZERO. "Naga" scores 388 but is a playable race in this build, not a tribe.

facts.claim: In this build the slave trade is present chiefly as the Empire's euphemism for it. The word "lease" outnumbers the word "slave" by roughly fifty to one.
in_world_sources: Ledger and Journal of Andrel Vorin
facts.measured: Counted over all of game/data on 2026-08-07: lease/Blackrose 2,240 hits; House Dres 245; slave/slavery 42; soul-gem or soul trade 15.

facts.claim: Does the soul of an Argonian who dies far from his own Hist reach it?

positions.in_world_source: The Grange Book (Archein Weighs-The-Rains)
positions.stance: Distance is nothing to a root. A man who dies at Tear is home before the letter is, and the tree is no poorer for the journey.
held_by: most of the Provincial Office by inheritance

positions.in_world_source: The Descents (kept at the rootpost, Lilmoth)
positions.stance: The nearest root still awake takes what it can reach. It is not his tree. He is issued out again a stranger, and the tree that made him is short by one in that year's count.
held_by: the Miredancers of the Eastern Rootlands

positions.in_world_source: Told at the Weir (Ranaso Quick-Tally, under-factor)
positions.stance: Distance costs. What comes back comes back short, the ground where he fell goes heavy, and there is no unit for how short.
held_by: the Agacephs of the Deep Marshes
the Naga-Kur, who carry their dead home at a price they pay in the open

facts.claim: Is the tree behind the wall on the Gideon estates a Hist of its own, or a cutting?

positions.in_world_source: The Grange Book (Archein Weighs-The-Rains)
positions.stance: Ours, and older than the Office. Entered on the survey as a Hist and tithed as a Hist. The wall went up over theft and not over shame.
held_by: the rootkeepers who have inspected it and signed

positions.in_world_source: Told at the Weir (Ranaso Quick-Tally, under-factor)
positions.stance: A cutting, carried off the Rootlands in a wet sack and put in a hole. It grows and it drinks and it holds nothing. The water under it runs clear, and clear means the root is going sideways.
held_by: most of the interior when the subject comes up

positions.in_world_source: Sap-Speaker Neekh-Otei, and the Miredancer elders with her
positions.stance: A true tree that has stopped answering, which is a third thing and worse than either of the other two.
held_by: the Sap-Speaker, who would rather it were a cutting

facts.claim: Is a hatchling given the sap from a vessel, away from the tree, given a soul?

positions.in_world_source: The Grange Book (Archein Weighs-The-Rains)
positions.stance: Sap is sap. Same tree, same hatchling, and the vessel is a vessel. The yard is also safer than the root, and half a wild hatching goes into the water.
held_by: the estate-hatched, who are the argument's own evidence

positions.in_world_source: The Descents (kept at the rootpost, Lilmoth)
positions.stance: The tree must be over it, with the roots under it, and it must see. What comes out of a cup is a body with something borrowed in it, and a loan has a term.
held_by: the Agacephs, who put it in one sentence and will not argue past it

positions.in_world_source: The burial figures of the Drowned Court at Soulrest
positions.stance: They get a soul and they come back short. The Court has the figures and the figures run four hundred years: estate-hatched and cup-given die a little young and bury a little heavy.
held_by: the sextons at Soulrest who keep the ledgers

facts.claim: Was the Duskfall one night, or generations?
in_world_sources: A Survey of the Peoples of the Interior

when.note: Undated in every in-world source and deliberately so. The dispute is about the SHAPE of the event, not its date, and no position here supplies a year.

positions.in_world_source: Xeeth of the Stone Forest, and the Sarpa generally
positions.stance: One night. Every stepped ruin in the province went over the same way, north-east shoulder first, and that can only be seen from the air.
held_by: one Imperial surveyor who has written it down and not published it

positions.in_world_source: The Descents (kept at the rootpost, Lilmoth)
positions.stance: Generations. The tablets change hand three times inside the falling, and a hand changes when a person dies.
held_by: the Sap-Speakers, who hold the tablets

positions.in_world_source: The Paatru of the Clay Moor
positions.stance: Three burnings, not one. The clay carries three black seams with clean clay between them, at the same depths anywhere on the moor.
held_by: anyone who has dug a pit on the Clay Moor in the dry season

facts.claim: Does the bone a Dead-Water warrior wears hold the dead back from the root?

positions.in_world_source: Dead-Water Koor-Nakh, at the Thorn gate
positions.stance: It holds her here and she fights. The shield turned twice and I was there for both.

positions.in_world_source: The Drowned Court at Soulrest
positions.stance: The pattern left at the moment of death. A bone is a bone after that — good bone, honoured bone, still bone. The Court has looked, professionally, for four hundred years.

positions.in_world_source: The Descents (kept at the rootpost, Lilmoth)
positions.stance: Nothing in the bone, and the going is delayed while the bone is above ground, and the delay is paid at the far end by somebody who was not asked.
held_by: the Sap-Speaker, who says it once and does not say it twice

facts.claim: What were the elevated stone walkways between the xanmeers built for?
in_world_sources: A Survey of the Peoples of the Interior

when.note: Built before the Duskfall by builders whose method is lost (CF-040). Every position here is an inference from wear, from a level, or from a memory nobody can date.

positions.in_world_source: Xeeth of the Stone Forest, and the Sarpa generally
positions.stance: Roosts. A hand and a half wide, running where no foot needs to go, worn on the outer edge where a claw sits. We were up there.

positions.in_world_source: Told at the Weir (Ranaso Quick-Tally, under-factor)
positions.stance: Roads. Door to door, with kerbs, and steps at both ends. Nothing flew.
held_by: every interior guide who has walked one

positions.in_world_source: A Survey of the Peoples of the Interior (Decius Arral, antiquarian)
positions.stance: Aqueducts. Eight runs measured with a level and a cord, each falling one part in four hundred along its whole length. A road does not need a fall.
held_by: the Gideon court, on Arral's authority and without reading him

facts.claim: The Agacephs of the Deep Marshes will not chase an animal, will not eat one that was chased, keep no sapwell, and will not give a direction — they take you, and you still do not learn the way.

The Paatru of the Clay Moor kill strangers in the wet season, because the clay holds the year's eggs; in the dry they trade at the moor's edge. They eat eggs that did not take, buried in clay. Their Hist is in a pit and they go down to it on a rope. They will not cross another people's bridge and they take nobody in.

The Sarpa of the Stone Forest eat carrion, keep a Hist that is a stump and say the true tree is overhead, weigh Imperial coin and drop it, and will not come down into a place they have not been asked into. They have seen every xanmeer in the province from above.

The Archein keep an estate Hist behind a wall and bring hatchlings sap in a copper cup; they eat Imperial food in courses from a written menu; they deal through a factor and never at the quay, and hold that distinction to be the whole of their honour.

The Miredancers name a Sap-Speaker who descends to the roots or the canopy, is fed only by the tree, and pays for it in gold tongue and bark-scale. The eighteenth Speaker has descended four times and brought back nothing, and will descend again.

The Dead-Water keep no Hist and drink at whichever tree they are nearest to; they take from other Argonian villages and are forgiven; they will not leave a body under any conditions; and it is they, not the weather, who close the tracks around Thorn.
